correctness.rationale: For the full directed strict refinement relation, the strict successor count is Bell(k)-1 and the strict predecessor count is the product of block Bell numbers minus one. Gluing two partitions at a shared point gives the injective and nonsurjective comparison Bell(p+q-1)>Bell(p)Bell(q) for p,q>=2, so repeated replacement of two nonsingleton sizes by (p+q-1,1) proves the unique maximizing one-nonsingleton size type. Round one identifies these witnesses, their sizes and their relation to the mark. For t<=b, the two pure witness families have round-two counts of one-step coarsenings strictly below the mark differing by (t-1)(b-a); these coarsenings have n-t>=3 blocks so none is accidentally the mark. For t>b the pure side is forced, and when b=1 the possible marked witness is already distinguished. In round three, pure two-point predecessor counts recover both positive mixed sizes using injectivity of binomial(s,2) on positive s; a mixed witness cannot equal a pure predecessor. For any nonwitness, all witnesses supported in a block count as strict predecessors. Their round-four counts give the binomial moments, whose missing low coefficients are k,a,b; translating variables recovers every block-profile multiplicity. The subgroup S_a times S_b is transitive on each profile and color invariance prohibits any further splitting or orbit fusion. Multiset enumeration and the labeled orbit count give the stated coefficient and class-size formulas. Independently generated all coarsenings directly for all 12 asymmetric pairs with a+b<=8, confirmed colors at round four and every class cardinality, including 57 and 97; no finite run is used to prove the round bound or its sharpness.
residual_risks: No optimal round bound shown; equal-size marks, Hasse-only edges and identification among arbitrary structures are out of scope.

value.rationale: This is a uniform depth bound independent of the Bell-sized domain for seeing a stabilizer's genuinely finer orbits. The side-orientation and moment-recovery steps explain how the mark changes the observable invariant, not simply the count of a few finite cases. It gives an explicit stopping depth for this natural family even though optimality is open within the record.
